title: Affine two-term determinant functors from good diagrams
statement: Fix coherent normalized derived pullback comparisons [lem-trf-two-term-determinant-pullback-coherence]. There exists an affine determinant system [def-trf-affine-determinant-interfaces]: finite projective two-term complexes give invertible determinant modules, every derived isomorphism acts by the kernel-normalized good-diagram map, and arbitrary affine scalar extension is natural and unital/associative. On pullbacks of displayed models from arbitrary schemes the exterior formula and zero trivialization form compatible families, and the identity complex has the evaluation normalization. This is only the affine algebra construction; it does not assert any determinant functor for non-affine schemes.

proof.text: Work first over a commutative ring $A$ with good complexes $P=[P^{-1}\to P^0]$ of finite projective modules. Set $D(P)=\det_A(P^0)\otimes\det_A(P^{-1})^\vee$ as in [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus]. It is invertible: on the finite free localizations of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover], wedge products of bases identify each top exterior power with $A$ (also for rank zero). Good complexes are bounded above with projective terms, so [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective] and [lem-coef-kprojective-derived-hom-bijection] identify their derived morphisms with chain maps modulo homotopy. In particular a derived isomorphism is represented by a quasi-isomorphism $a:P\to Q$ and has a chain-map inverse up to homotopy. The surjective case already has the explicit map $T_a$ of the new calculus lemma.

For an arbitrary quasi-isomorphism $a:P\to Q$, choose a finite free module $F$ and a surjection $p:F\to Q^{-1}$. Let $M=[P^{-1}\oplus F\xrightarrow{d_P\oplus1}P^0\oplus F]$, let $b:M\to P$ be projection, and put $c^{-1}=(a^{-1},p)$ and $c^0=(a^0,d_Qp)$. Then $c$ is a chain map homotopic to $ab$ by $h(x,f)=p(f)$ in degree zero. The kernel of $b$ is $[F\xrightarrow{1}F]$, so $b$ and $c$ are quasi-isomorphisms. The map $c^{-1}$ is surjective. Given $y\in Q^0$, surjectivity of $H^0(a)$ writes $y=a^0(x)+d_Q(z)$; lift $z$ through $p$ to see that $c^0$ is surjective. Hence both $b,c$ qualify for [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus]. For any such good diagram (allowing $c\simeq ab$) define its proposed map to be $T_cT_b^{-1}:D(P)\to D(Q)$.

For a good diagram for $1_P$, its two legs are homotopic, and the homotopy clause of [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus] makes $T_cT_b^{-1}=1$. Next take good diagrams $(b_{12},c_{12})$ for $a:P_1\to P_2$ and $(b_{23},c_{23})$ for $a':P_2\to P_3$. Form the degreewise fibre product $N=M_{12}\times_{P_2}M_{23}$, along $c_{12},b_{23}$, with projections $r,s$. Each projection is surjective; its kernel is the kernel complex of the other surjective leg, hence has an isomorphism as differential. The exact sequence on terms splits since the quotient terms are projective, so $N$ has finite projective terms. The projections are quasi-isomorphisms: a cycle lifts after correcting its differential using the acyclic kernel, and a lift of a boundary differs from a boundary by a kernel cycle, which is a kernel boundary. Thus $(b_{12}r,c_{23}s)$ is a good diagram for $a'a$. The equality $c_{12}r=b_{23}s$ and the composition clause of the calculus lemma give $T_{c_{12}}T_r=T_{b_{23}}T_s$. Rearranging yields $T_{c_{23}s}T_{b_{12}r}^{-1}=(T_{c_{23}}T_{b_{23}}^{-1})(T_{c_{12}}T_{b_{12}}^{-1})$.

Fix a homotopy inverse $a':Q\to P$ of $a$ from [lem-coef-kprojective-derived-hom-bijection] and fix one good diagram for $a'$. Compose it with any good diagram for $a$ using the preceding fibre product. Since $a'a\simeq1_P$, the resulting legs are homotopic; step 4 makes its map the identity. Thus every proposed map for $a$ equals the inverse of the fixed map for $a'$, proving independence of good diagram. A good diagram for $a$ is also one for any homotopic representative, so the map depends only on the derived morphism. Step 4 now proves the composition law, and its identity calculation proves the identity law. Transport along identifications of a model with a derived object gives the determinant functor and its canonical comparisons between models: the comparison for a composite identification is the composite comparison, by this same law.

For a ring map $A\to B$, the map $B\otimes_A\bigwedge^r V\to\bigwedge^r(B\otimes_A V)$ sends $b\otimes(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_r)$ to $b((1\otimes v_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge(1\otimes v_r))$. It is an isomorphism for finite projective $V$: check on the free localizations of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover], where basis wedges give its inverse. Likewise $B\otimes_A V^\vee\cong(B\otimes_A V)^\vee$ is checked on a finite basis. These formulas give $B\otimes_A D(P)\cong D(B\otimes_A P)$. A surjective good map has split exact term sequences and kernel differential an isomorphism, so tensoring preserves its defining kernel sequences and quasi-isomorphism. The wedge-lift maps $\gamma^i$ and $\delta_N=\det(d_N)$ in [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus] commute with this scalar extension, directly by their displayed wedge formulas. Consequently $T_a$ commutes with scalar extension for surjective maps, and $T_cT_b^{-1}$ does so for all good diagrams. Identities and iterated scalar extension agree because both maps send a pure wedge tensor to the same wedge tensor. This also proves naturality in derived isomorphisms. No flatness of $A\to B$ is required.

The preceding scalar-extension formula computes derived extension of scalars on good complexes. Indeed a finite projective module is flat: tensoring with it is a direct summand of tensoring with a finite free module, so preserves exactness. By [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], a good complex is K-flat, hence ordinary tensor computes its derived tensor. In the special model $P=[V\xrightarrow{1}V]$, apply the surjective-map construction of [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus] to $P\to0$. Its kernel is $P$, $\delta_P=\det(1_V)$, and the short-exact-sequence maps for quotient zero are identities. Thus $D(P)\to A$ takes $\det(1_V)$ to $1$. Under the ordinary symmetry identifying $D(P)$ with $(\det V)^\vee\otimes\det V$, this is exactly evaluation. This includes $V=0$.

Transport the affine module construction through the affine derived equivalence and the affine tensor comparison. For a model on an arbitrary scheme, pull its terms to an affine test scheme; the pure-wedge scalar-extension formulas give the local_modelIso family. Iteration proves local_model_naturality. The rank-zero formulas give local_zeroIso and its naturality. The actual acyclic identity complex is zero in the derived category, and the contraction calculation on every affine test scheme proves local_acyclic.

mathlib_searches.query: determinant functor two term perfect complexes invertible sheaf pullback
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits about free module pullback isomorphisms; none constructs determinant functors or affine descent. For the Tor-window search, DerivedCategory.exists_iso_Q_obj_of_isGE_of_isLE gives a cohomologically bounded complex, without finite locally free terms. The existing finite-free residue model in our library supplies the stronger input.
Zero hits. The separate "Perfect", "Tor" query returned unrelated perfect groups, perfect closures and graph matchings.

Two hits in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Complex/Determinant.lean concern complex numbers, not complexes. The additional leftAdjointCompIso search found the mate/composition API used in the proved normalized-coherence argument. No determinant construction was found.

mathlib_searches.query: Determinant line of two term perfect complexes compatible with affine base change and descent
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: LinearMap.det, IsBaseChange.det_endHom, LinearEquiv.det_baseChange, LinearMap.det_baseChange and related scalar determinants. These are endomorphism determinants, not determinant lines of complexes or compatible gluing data. The queried theorem types do not provide the required construction.

    [∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens),
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (κ : TwoTermDeterminantPullbackCoherence.{u, w}) :
    Nonempty (AffineTwoTermDeterminantData κ)
